content: The following are the detailed steps for donning personal protective equipment (PPE), including a gown, as outlined by the World Health Organization (WHO). The responsibility for interpreting and using this material lies with the reader. 1. Begin by removing all personal items, such as jewelry, watches, cell phones, and pens, to prevent contamination. 2. In the changing room, put on a scrub suit and rubber boots. If boots are unavailable, wear closed shoes that are slip-on (without shoelaces), fully cover the dorsum of the foot and ankles, and are paired with non-slip, preferably impermeable, shoe covers. 3. Move to the clean area located at the entrance of the isolation unit. 4. 5. 6. Perform hand hygiene thoroughly before proceeding. 7. Put on a face mask to protect the respiratory system. 8. Wear a disposable waterproof apron. If a disposable apron is unavailable, use a heavy-duty, reusable waterproof apron. 9. Put on a face shield or goggles to protect the eyes. 10. Cover the head and neck with a surgical bonnet that extends to cover the neck and sides of the head. If possible, use a bonnet that integrates with the face shield. Alternatively, a hood may be used. 11. These steps are critical to minimizing the risk of contamination and ensuring the safety of healthcare workers in high-risk environments.
